questions.question: The International Kite Festival in Gujarat is held in the month of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**January.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The International Kite Festival in Gujarat is held in the month of **January.**__
 
• Every year the International Kite Festival is organized in Gujarat on the occasion of Uttarayan i.e. Makar Sankranti.
 
• Tourists come from all over the country and abroad to take part in this kite festival.
 
• Apart from Ahmedabad, you can see this festival in other cities of Gujarat such as Surat, Vadodara, and Rajkot.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The International Kite Festival started in 1989.
 
• On the occasion of Uttarayan, when the weather is changing, winter decreases and summer starts.
 
• At such a time, the main purpose of organizing a kite festival is to share happiness among the people.
 
• Since 1989, the International Kite Festival is held every year in Ahmedabad.​

questions.question: Who among the following is an architect credited with planning and designing major parts of New Delhi’s buildings during the British period?

questions.question: Garia Puja of Tripura is celebrated for how many days in April?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Garia Puja is one of the main festivals of Tripura.
 
• Garia Puja is a festival celebrated in the third week of April. 
 
• Lord Garia, the deity of livestock and wealth, is worshipped with flowers and garland during this festival.
 
• The Garia Puja is conducted with these ingredients: cotton thread, rice, fowl chick, rice beer, wine, earthen pots, eggs, and wine.
 
• It involves an old age tradition of sacrificing the fowl before the deity, and to get the blessings of the Lord, the blood of the fowl is sprayed before the Lord.
 
• While the festival is being celebrated, no one is allowed to cross the shadow of the bamboo tree, which is symbolic god Garia, due to the fear of annoying the Lord.
 
• The festival witnesses the children playing the drums, singing, and dancing before Lord Garia in order to appease him.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• About Tripura:

 
 
• Kharchi Festival, Ker Puja, Bizu Festival, Tirtha Mukh Festival, Ashokastami, Ganga Puja, Lampra Puja, Wah festival are important festivals of Tripura.
 
• Capital: Agartala.
 
• Chief Minister: **Manik Saha**.
 
• Governor: **Shri Indrasena Reddy Nallu.**
 
• Official Language: Kokborok, English, Bengali.

questions.question: Hurka Baul is a dance form prevalent in the state of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Uttarakhand.____ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Hurka Baul is a dance form prevalent in the state of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• The Hurkiya Baul dance is done in the fields while paddy and maize are being grown.
 
• After executing the preceding ceremony on a set day, the dance is done in several fields to various tunes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The dance is named after the Hurka, which is the drum that provides musical accompaniment to the dance, and Baul, which is the song.
 
• The only musical instrument used in the dance is the hurka.
 
• The singer relates the story of conflicts and heroic acts slowly and interestingly in the Hurka Baul dance performance. The actors usually arrive from two directions and execute the story in a sequence of snappy motions and appealing dancing styles.
 
• Other important dance forms of Uttarakhand are
 
 
• **Pandav** Nritya, 
 
• Bhotia Dance, 
 
• Cholia Dance,

questions.question: In which of the following states is Kolannalu dance form performed?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Kolannalu dance **form performed in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• This is a stick dance and a very popular dance in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The dance form was originated in the Seventh century.
 
• This dance form has various names, in various regions of India. In Andhra Pradesh, this dance called as KolKollannalu, Kolattam and Kolannalu.
 
• In the early days, the dance was performed by women only, gradually the changes occurred in this dance and now the dance was performed by both male and female.
 
• The dance is the combination of rhythmic movements, songs, and music.
 
• The dance is performed by 8 to 40 artists as a group and every two artists grouped as a pair.
 
• Each one holds the two sticks and moves the sticks according to their leader movements.

questions.question: Which form of dance involves balancing pots on the head of the dancer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhavai.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhavai form of dance involves balancing pots on the head of the dancer.**
 
• Bhavai Dance is a very difficult form of dance performed by skilled experts.
 
• In this dance, women dancers balance 8 to 9 pitchers on their heads and dance simultaneously.
 
• And sway with the soles of their feet perched on the top of a glass and also sometimes on the edge of a naked sword.
 
• This dance is believed to be originated in Gujarat.
 
• And was soon picked up and adopted by the local tribal men and women of Rajasthan.
 
• This is basically performed by the women of the Jat, Bhil, Raigar, Meena, Kumhar, and Kalbelia communities of Rajasthan.
 
• **Main instruments:**
 
 
• Dholak, Jhanjhar, Pakhwaja, Sarangi, and Harmonium (played in background music).
 
• The government is taking all necessary measures to revive this fast-dying tradition of folk dance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cheraw:**

 
 
• It is one of the traditional and oldest dances of Mizoram.
 
• It is also recognized as the oldest dance form of Mizoram.
 
• It is also known as the Bamboo dance.
 
• It is one of the most famous dances in Mizoram, and a centre of attraction during festive occasions.
 
• Chewar is performed by six to eight people holding a pair of bamboo staves on another horizontally placed bamboo on the ground on special occasions such as when there is a bumper harvest of a crop. Gongs and drums are used as a musical instruments in Cheraw dance.
 
 
 
• **Deodhani:**
 
 
• It is a dance form of Assam.

questions.question: The ‘Kalpataru Utsav’ is held on the first of ______ every year.
questions.solution:

• **Kalpataru Utsav** is an annual religious festival observed by** monks of the Ramakrishna Mission** on the **1st of January every year.**
 
• Kalpataru Utsav** marks the metamorphosis of Ramakrishna Paramahansa into a Kalpataru or magical tree **and the 'Kalpataru Day' or 'Kalpataru Diwas'.
 
• A large number of** devotees move into the Dakshineshwar Kali Temple to celebrate the Kalpataru Utsav** every year.
 
• **The Dakshineswar Kali temple is located on the eastern bank of the Hooghly River** and it is devoted to the Goddess Kali as well as Lord Shiva.
 
• **Ramakrishna Paramahansa **passed a considerable amount of his life,** serving the deity Kali, in this temple.**
 
• The religious event is observed on 1st January 1886 and it is on this very auspicious day that the **disciples of Ramakrishna Paramhansa believe that he had manifested himself to be a divine avatar, or 'God incarnate on earth.​**

questions.question: 'Machail Mata' shrine located in the Kishtwar district of Jammu is dedicated to the Goddess :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Durga__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Goddess Durga shrine called Machail Chandi Mata Temple** is also known as Machail Mata. It is located in the village of Machail of Sub Division Paddar in the Indian union territory of **Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar District**, where it gets its name.
 
• The **best time to visit Machail Mata Temple** is during the Machail Yatra (15 & 16 August), which is held in the month of August. Between March and November, **devotees can also go to the temple.**
 
• The shrine, also known as **Machail mata Sthan,** offers a breathtaking environment with hills, glaciers, and Chenab River tributaries. Nearby **Paddar Valley** is well-known for its **renowned sapphire mining **and is a nice location for trekking, cannoning, and holy hot **springs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** territory, which is populated by a Buddhist **group and the serpent-worshipping Thakur community, was amalgamated with Kishtwar tehsil by **Maharaja Ranbir Singh. **
 
• **The shrine has an ancient beginning** and no known past. The goddess made her** "swayambhu" **appearance in such a remote location.
 
• **She originally manifested as a fiery flame** in the village of Mindhal in the Pangi Valley, 60 kilometres from Machail, and later as Singhasan Mata (Saraswati) in the village of Chitto (which is 15 km from Gulabgarh). Later, the fire took on the **shape of Pindi.**
 
• The** genuine temple in Machail village is a swayambhu** with three idols of Mahakali (Mindal), Mahalakshmi (Machail), and Mahasaraswati, together with** one pindi and this shrine** (Chitto Mata).

questions.question: In the context of Bhakti-Sufi traditions of India, Manikkavachakar, a devotee of ______, composed beautiful devotional songs in Tamil.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shiva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manikkavachakar **or **Maanikka Vaasagar **was a** 9th-century Tamil poet **who wrote **Tiruvasakam**, a book of **Shiva’s hymns.**
 
• He was one of the major writers of Saivite Thirumurai.
 
• He was the principal adherent of the Nayanars traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Nayanars**
 **Alvars**
 
 

 Nayanars were devoted to Lord Shiva and his Avatars
 Alvars were devoted to Lord Vishnu and his Avatars
 
 

 Nayanars were active around the 6th-8th Century AD
 Although modern scholars consider the Alvars to be active between the 5th and 10th century AD, they are believed to have lived between 4200 BCE - 2700 BCE.
 
 

 The high priest of Raja Raja Chola I, Nambiyandar Nambi, compiled the hymn into a series of volumes called the thirumurai.
 The hymns of Alvars were made into a consolidated volume known as Divya Prabandha
 
 

 There were 63 Nayanars, who belonged to different caste backgrounds such as potters, “untouchable” workers, peasants, hunters, soldiers, Brahmanas, and chiefs.
 There were 12 Alvars, who came from equally divergent backgrounds, the best known being Periyalvar, his daughter Andal, Tondaradippodi Alvar and Nammalvar.
